summary: Collects enterprise use cases for gathering configuration and operational data from endpoints and evaluating it to judge an organization's security posture. The use cases are meant to reveal common requirements for vendor-neutral, interoperable standards. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: A school checks that every computer has its locks closed. This lists the situations where that checking would be useful.

questions: what is endpoint security posture assessment
what are the use cases for security posture assessment
what are security automation use cases
subtitle: Use cases for collecting data from endpoints and checking it against policy, as groundwork for common standards.

tldr.problem: Organizations assess the security posture of their endpoints with tools that cannot easily share data, so the work is hard to automate across vendors.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes a typical assessment workflow, four use cases built from reusable building blocks (publish and query data, plan, collect, evaluate), and seven usage scenarios that show them in practice.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational memo whose use cases are meant to yield requirements, an information model and an architecture for vendor-neutral, interoperable standards.

today: RFC 7632 is an Informational document and has not been obsoleted or updated. It describes use cases and does not define a protocol.

sections.title: Goal and Scope
sections.content:
This memo documents core use cases for endpoint posture assessment in enterprises. They support securely collecting and aggregating configuration and operational data, and evaluating that data to determine the security posture of individual endpoints. Seven usage scenarios then show how the use cases and their building blocks address different operational functions.

From these, the working group can derive common concepts, requirements, an information model and an architecture, which are meant to guide vendor-neutral, interoperable standards. Common data formats should let tools, whether custom, commercial or free, interoperate and automate parts of security processes. The output is expected to feed policy-based enforcement, verification of security controls and regulatory compliance. Enterprise and service-provider use cases are expected to overlap, though service providers face extra complications when information crosses administrative domains.
sections.plainLanguage: Write down the situations where checking computers for safety matters, so people can design a shared way to do it.

sections.title: The Assessment Workflow
sections.content:
Endpoint posture assessment means collecting an endpoint's attributes, making them available for evaluation and action, and verifying that the endpoint complies with enterprise standards and policy.

The typical workflow is:

  1. A trigger starts it, such as an operator request, an application or an event notification from the endpoint.
  2. An operator or application selects target endpoints and the applicable policies.
  3. For each target, it decides which posture attributes to collect, may use cached data such as an asset management system, and may collect from the target itself or from intermediaries or agents, mutually authenticating where appropriate.
  4. An evaluator compares the collected attributes with the expected values in policy and reports the result in a standardized or proprietary form, such as a report, log entry, database entry or notification.

Implementations should support mixed sets of standardized and proprietary attributes.
sections.plainLanguage: Something says 'time to check', you pick which computers and which rules, gather the facts, compare them to the rules, and write down the result.

sections.title: Four Use Cases and Their Building Blocks
sections.content:
Each use case lists the building blocks, or capabilities, it needs.

  • Define, publish, query and retrieve security automation data. This data falls into three categories: guidance (instructions and policies that drive collection and evaluation, shared widely and changing over months or days), attribute data (endpoint characterizations and collected values, organization-specific and usually access-controlled) and processing artifacts (data specific to one assessment). Building blocks are Data Definition, Publication, Query, Retrieval and Change Detection.
  • Endpoint identification and assessment planning. Endpoint Discovery, Characterization, Target Identification, Component Inventory and Posture Attribute Identification.
  • Posture attribute value collection. Collection Guidance Acquisition and Posture Attribute Value Collection, triggered by an endpoint event, a network event such as connecting to a VPN, or a scheduled or ad hoc task.
  • Posture attribute evaluation. Collected Posture Change Detection, Posture Attribute Value Query, Evaluation Guidance Acquisition and Posture Attribute Evaluation, which compares actual against expected values. The same blocks can support trending and historic analysis.
sections.plainLanguage: The big jobs are split into small reusable steps, like finding computers, collecting facts and comparing them to the rules. Different tools can then each do one step.

sections.title: Usage Scenarios
sections.content:
The scenarios show the blocks in use:

  • Publishing configuration checklists: a vendor publishes automatable checklists for its devices to a public data store.
  • Automated checklist verification: a financial services company gathers its software inventory, retrieves the right checklists, collects the settings and evaluates actual against expected state.
  • Detecting posture deviations: an endpoint is checked against its baseline and then monitored, so a change triggers an alert and only the change is assessed.
  • Analysis and reporting: an administrator who sees five endpoints uploading data to a suspicious server queries stored posture data to find every endpoint with the same program.
  • Ice Station Zebra: a university team in the Arctic has only an intermittent, low-speed, high-latency, high-cost satellite link, so collection requests and results are batched and guidance is cached locally.
  • Guidance identification and retrieval, and guidance change detection: finding, caching and being told about new, updated or deleted guidance.
sections.plainLanguage: Examples include a company checking all its computers against a rulebook and a research team in the Arctic with very slow internet that sends its checks in batches.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The memo only documents use cases, so specific security and privacy considerations are left to the related requirements, architecture, information model, data model and protocol documents. It does warn that a malicious actor could use the security automation infrastructure and collected data to reach personal data, private keys, or software and configuration state that could inform an attack.

It says communications between components should consider confidentiality, data integrity and peer entity authentication, and that exchanged information should have an authenticatable origin so provenance can be tracked. Systems storing sensitive data need protection against unauthorized use, inappropriate use and denial of service.
sections.plainLanguage: A list of every computer's weak spots would be a gift to a burglar, so the system that collects it must be well locked.
